messages:
Support Ops: heads-up — we got a Priority 2 from AcmeApp about a sudden p99 spike on /v1/generate yesterday evening (customer-facing latency complaints). They sent a flamegraph and said errors are low but tail latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s.
Maria K: thanks. any recent rollout to the continuous-batcher or routing changes?
Support Ops: no deploys at the time, but customer noted it aligns with a config tweak one of their tenants made to batcher timeout and max_batch_size we rolled last week. they sent our snippet.
Ajay P: which change? we shipped the new continuous-batcher config defaults 6 days ago: `batch_timeout_ms: 60 -> 120` and `max_batch_size: 64 -> 128` as an opt-in perf tweak.
Lee (oncall): grabbing graphs now (prom query). high-level: p50 ~200ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 jumps near 1.1-1.3s across that route cluster. spike correlates with increased probability of large batches during short bursts.
Lee (oncall): here's the prom query I ran: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))`
Maria K: that suggests batching wait time is contributing to tail. If batch_timeout_ms increased, single-request latency could be dominated by wait-to-fill window when traffic is bursty.
Jordan: AcmeApp is on Dedicated, but uses our continuous-batcher. They pushed config change upstream to make use of higher max_batch_size; maybe their request pattern made more waiting.
Ajay P: two angles: 1) configuration defaults we promoted may be too aggressive, 2) the batcher has a pathological case: when max_batch_size is large AND burstiness present, the batcher will wait up to batch_timeout_ms trying to fill the batch, increasing tail latency for small requests.
Support Ops: customer asked for mitigation steps — they need something quick (they're in production).
Maria K: immediate mitigations: lower batch_timeout_ms for that tenant to 30ms or set max_batch_size back to 64. Also enable prefix caching for their common short prompts.
Lee (oncall): I'm running a quick canary rollback of batch_timeout for that tenant to 40ms via the tenant override API.
sre-bot: action: tenant-config-update completed for tenant acmeapp (batch_timeout_ms:120->40) — job id tcfg-20260312-09
Lee (oncall): canary applied. Waiting for a 10-min window to collect metrics.
(6 minutes later)
Lee (oncall): preliminary metrics: p99 down from 1.25s -> 360ms on the affected hosts. p95 also improved to ~400ms. Looks promising.
Jordan: can we get the customer to validate?
Support Ops: pinged them. They confirm lower tail and better UX — thank you.
Ajay P: root cause summary for the postmortem: interaction of increased `batch_timeout_ms` and `max_batch_size` defaults with bursty request arrival patterns caused higher waiting time for small bursty requests. The continuous-batcher's adaptive early-flush heuristic didn't trigger in cases where request rate had high variance.
Maria K: long-term fixes we should consider: 1) make early-flush more aggressive when batch fill rate is low (decay based on recent inter-arrival times), 2) add tenant-level safety caps that prevent promoting both high timeout and large max batch size simultaneously without explicit approval, 3) expose a per-route latency SLO monitor that auto-suggests safer batch configs.
Ajay P: also add a new metric: `batch_wait_ms` per-batch quantiles and per-tenant breakdown so we can correlate wait time -> tail latency quickly.
Lee (oncall): I'll file the follow-up tickets and attach the prom/honeycomb slices.
Maria K: include a small repro harness we can run locally that simulates bursty arrivals. attached snippet:
```bash
# repro script (python, quick): send bursts of 1-3 requests with short gaps
for burst in range(100):
  for i in range(3):
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' &
  sleep 0.02
wait
```
Maria K: run against a local batcher with `batch_timeout_ms=120` and `max_batch_size=128` to see the increase in per-request latency at the p99.
Ajay P: I'll also add a unit test that simulates a Poisson burst arrival and asserts p99 under candidate changes to early-flush.
Jordan: for customer comms we should: 1) summarize root cause, 2) note immediate mitigation we applied (tenant override), 3) ETA for permanent fix (2 weeks for heuristics + 4 weeks for tenant-safety features).
Support Ops: customer happy with that plan. They've asked for a config doc to help tuned batching for their workloads.
Maria K: assigning ownership: Ajay -> early-flush heuristic (PR & unit tests), Lee -> tenant override safety caps + alerting, Jordan -> customer-facing doc + follow-up comms, Maria -> postmortem and rollout notes.
Lee (oncall): filing ops tickets now: OPS-4521 (tenant safety caps), OPS-4522 (batch_wait_ms metric), ENG-9987 (early-flush heuristic).
(End)
